title: Skullmonkeys
subtitle: Klaymen trades puzzles for platforms
summary: Skullmonkeys is The Neverhood, Inc.'s PlayStation platform game, first released in North America on 6 February 1998. body: Skullmonkeys is The Neverhood, Inc.'s PlayStation platform game, first released in North America on 6 February 1998. Klaymen returns from The Neverhood to confront creatures controlled by his old enemy Klogg, but the earlier adventure's pointing and clicking gives way to running and jumping. Sculpted clay characters and scenery retain the world's handmade appearance. The player moves through a succession of strange places whose humour often arrives through a face, sound or unexpected movement. Its identity comes as much from how those objects were made as from the route through each level.

Klaymen can defeat enemies by landing on them, while collected weapons offer other ways to remove a threat. A halo allows him to survive an additional hit, making the next mistake less final. Secret areas provide bonus points and extra lives, rewarding attention to the edges of the main route. The side-scrolling structure keeps the task clear even when the world becomes increasingly absurd. The player reads a familiar platforming problem through unfamiliar materials, with clay figures and deliberately odd details giving a conventional jump a different personality.

Terry Scott Taylor composed music that supports the game's comic and unsettling atmosphere, including deliberately relaxed material for its bonus stages. The same commitment to a particular tone connects Skullmonkeys to The Neverhood despite the change of genre. Reviews praised the clay-based appearance and music while finding less variety in the underlying play. The European release followed in February 1998. The game remains a distinctive PlayStation object because its visual world appears physically constructed, preserving the marks of a craft process inside a machine associated with the arrival of three-dimensional graphics.
story_headings: Jump first, then use the stranger tools
A soundtrack as unusual as the scenery
